gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 70mai A400 has a micro-USB power port and so takes only the UP02 hardwire kit for parking mode (not the USB-C UP03 that rivals name for other 70mai cameras), that 70mai's own store showed the UP02 as unavailable on 2026-11-21, or that the A400's card limit is 128 GB.
standout_why: Compared against carcody.com (cited), rottenwifi.com (cited) and dealdey.com (rank 1). dashanddrive.com (cited in chat 2) would not open (certificate error), so it was not compared. Carcody and RottenWifi both say the A400 needs 70mai's 'separately sold hardwire kit' and the RC09 rear camera, but give no kit model, kit price, power-port type, stock status, RC09 price or card limit. Both name the UP03 only for the M310. Both mention an optional VIOFO hardwire kit without the HK4 name, its price or its mini-USB exclusion. DealDey gives no kit model, no card maximum and no cable type for any camera. None of the three covers the Vantrue S1 Pro, so none has its kit pairing or 512 GB card limit.
decides: It changes the pick only for shoppers who want parking mode; for driving-only use the A400 stays the cheapest pick. With the RC09 rear camera it is $59.98 at 70mai's store, but its parking kit (UP02, $28.99) showed as unavailable there on 2026-11-21, the USB-C UP03 does not fit, and its card limit is 128 GB. The Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH ($79.99, a partner store we can link) takes a kit that is in stock and supports 512 GB cards, but camera plus that kit is $109.98, over the budget line. The VIOFO A119 Mini 2 is $159.99 at viofo.com today, so it is out on budget before any kit. The brief's partner table lists DDPAI camera-plus-hardwire-kit variants under $100 (N1 Dual + kit $89, MINI PRO 4K + kit $69); I did not open those variant pages, but if they hold, DDPAI is the parking-mode route that stays under $100 through a partner link.
